title: Romania – Cleaning services – Servicii de curatenie la pasajele administrate de Administratia Strazilor Bucuresti
description: Pentru buna desfașurare a activității specifice Administrației Străzilor București (ASB), pentru menținerea curațeniei și a condițiilor impuse de igienă a pasajelor, este necesară achiziția de servicii de curățenie la pasajele aflate în administrarea ASB. Obiectul actual cuprinde pasajele Universității, Basarab, Piața Presei Libere, Piața Sudului — inclusiv pasajul către metrou și pasajul Secuilor — și pasajul pietonal Lipscani. Față de documentația contractuală anterioară, modificările privesc includerea celor două pasaje noi de la Piața Sudului, introducerea operațiunilor distincte de curățare și dezinfectare a interiorului lifturilor și de spălare a treptelor scărilor rulante de la Basarab, precum și definirea distinctă a operațiunilor de deszăpezire, evacuare a zăpezii și împrăștiere a materialului antiderapant. Spălarea geamurilor escalatoarelor și curățarea inoxului scărilor rulante de la Basarab sunt operațiuni istorice. Pasajul pietonal Lipscani era inclus în prestația anterioară; deszăpezirea scărilor sale de acces nu mai face obiectul noului acord-cadru. Programul actual este extins: 24 din 24 de ore de vineri până duminică la Pasajul Universității și la Pasajul pietonal Lipscani, grupurile sanitare de la Pasajul Universității 24 din 24 de ore, 7 zile din 7, iar Pasajul Basarab zilnic între orele 08:00 și 22:00.

title: Dielectric Coated Optics
description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION FOR COMMERCIAL ITEMS This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) subpart 12.6, "Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Items," as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested, and a written solicitation document will not be issued. This solicitation is a Request for Quotations (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 Effective: 03/13/2026. This is a Total Small Business Set-Aside in accordance with FAR 13.003 (b)(1) on a Firm-Firm Fixed-Price (FFP) basis. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 333310 with a small business size standard of 1000. The associated Federal Supply Code (FSC) / Product Service Code (PSC) procurement is 6650. No remanufactured or "gray market" items are acceptable. All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer's warranty. � Vendor shall be an Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), an OEM authorized dealer, an authorized distributor, or an authorized reseller for the proposed equipment/system such that OEM warranty and service are provided and maintained by the OEM. All software licensing, warranty, and service associated with the equipment/system shall be in accordance with the OEM terms and conditions � Offerors are required to submit documentation from the manufacturer stating that they are an authorized distributor for the specific items being procured. Note: Maintenance Renewals - The performance period for maintenance renewals, (software licenses, services, etc.), must begin on or after the date of contract award. The performance period cannot be back dated. If reinstatement fees are required, they must be listed on separate line items. Delivery Address: X U.S. Naval Research Laboratory 4555 Overlook Avenue, S.W. Bldg. 49 � Shipping/Receiving Code 3400 Washington, DC 20375 **FOB DESTINATION IS THE PREFERRED METHOD** Estimated Delivery Time: __________________ For FOB ORGIN, please provide the following information: FOB Shipping Point: _______________________ Estimated Shipping Charge: _________________ Dimensions of Package(s): ____________________ Shipping Weight: __________________________ SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: All Quoters shall submit 1 (one) copy of their technical and price quote. Include your company DUNS Number and Cage Code on your quote. All quotations shall be sent via e-mail. GOVERNMENT POINT OF CONTACT Purchasing Agent Name: Elizabeth Harley Email: elizabeth.c.harley.civ@us.navy.mil Please reference this combined synopsis/solicitation number on your correspondence and in the "Subject" line of your email. ALL QUESTIONS REGARDING THE SOLICITATION SHALL BE SUBMITTED VIA EMAIL. The government intends to award a purchase order as a result of this combined synopsis/solicitation that will include the terms and conditions set forth herein. Award may be made without discussions or negotiations, therefore prospective contractors should have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) database (www.sam.gov) in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 4.1102 and Part 52.204-7 when submitting a response to this solicitation. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers: Lowest Price Technically Acceptable - Offers will be ranked lowest to highest according to price. A price analysis will be conducted to determine whether the lowest price will result from a single award or multiple awards. Based on the price analysis, the lowest price offer or multiple offers, will be forwarded to the requiring activity for technical evaluation (offer(s), in accordance with the specifications, will be deemed either technically acceptable or technically unacceptable). If the lowest price offer or offers is found technically acceptable and the pricing determined fair and reasonable by the Contracting Officer, evaluation will be deemed complete and award will be made based on the lowest price offer(s). If the lowest price offer is determined technically unacceptable, another analysis will be conducted amongst the remaining offers to determine if a single or multiple awards will provide the lowest price. The lowest price offer(s) will be sent for technical evaluation. This process is repeated in order of price until an offer or combination of offers is deemed technically acceptable and price is determined fair and reasonable. Table A-1. Technical Acceptable/Unacceptable Ratings: Rating Description Acceptable Quote meets all the minimum requirements/specifications as stated or provided in the RFQ specifications. Unacceptable Quote does not clearly meet the minimum requirements/specifications as stated or provided in the RFQ specifications. Options. When applicable, the Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total price for all options to the total price for the basic requirement. The Government may determine that an offer is unacceptable if the option prices are significantly unbalanced. Evaluation of options shall not obligate the Government to exercise the option(s). Terms and Conditions. To facilitate the award process, all quotes must include a statement regarding the terms and conditions herein as follows: "The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award document without modification, deletion, or addition." description: Pre-Solicitation Synopsis In accordance with RFO 5.204, this pre-solicitation notice is meant to inform industry of an anticipated, upcoming solicitation. This notice will not bind the government to any actions or awards. DESCRIPTION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Louisville District intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) W912QR26RA056 for Janitorial Services for multiple recruiting stations throughout the states of Oklahoma, Texas, Arkansas, and Louisiana. The work includes management, supervision, inspection, personnel, equipment, tools, supplies, materials, transportation, and other items necessary to perform janitorial services as described in the schedule of janitorial services for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers leased space. Janitorial service applies to all designated spaces, including, but not limited to halls, restrooms, offices, work areas, entranceways, lobbies, common areas, test room areas, and storage room areas. The period of performance will be a base period of twelve (12) months with four (4) option periods. Each option period will be for twelve (12) months. Behang und Mulde - 1 Gefriertruhe für Körperteile mit Temperaturüberwachung - 2 Standleuchter (Elektrokerzen) Die Lieferung und Montage der Bestandteile soll nach dem folgenden Prioritäten-Schema getrennt ablaufen: Montage Unterkonstruktionen, Montage Leichenkühlzellanlagen, Lieferung Zubehör unmittelbar vor Inbetriebnahme (Diebstahlprävention). 1 Haupt- und 1 Nachbesserungstermin sind mit dem Angebotspreis abgegolten, wobei die Teilleistungen gemäß Terminplan gestaffelt einzutakten und mit der örtlichen Bauleitung/Fachbauleitung abzustimmen sind. Die gesetzliche Verjährungsfrist der Gewährleistungsansprüche beginnt mit der Abnahme der Leistung. Der Tag der Abnahme (komplette Montage inklusive Mängelbeseitigungen) ist der Gewährleistungsbeginn. Folgende Leistungen sind neben den gerätebezogenen Leistungen anzubieten und zu kalkulieren: - Bei der Kollisionsprüfung durch den koordinierenden Architekten (4Bund) ist durch den Auftragnehmer (AN) mitzuwirken. Die Montagepläne sind bei Erfordernis anzupassen. - Für Organisationsbesprechungen - auch teil- und abschnittsweise - hat der AN einen mit der Anlage in allen Teilen technisch und betrieblich vertrauten, sachkundigen Mitarbeiter beizustellen. - Weitere Leitungen gemäß den zusätzlichen technischen Vorbemerkungen der Medizintechnik. Eignungskriterien gemäß allgemeinen und besonderen Vertragsbedingungen, Punkt 1.10 / Punkt 2.10 Für die Lieferungen und Montagen der Geräte sind folgende Termine maßgebend: Möglicher Beginn Einbau: 24.09.2027 Spätester Abschluss Montagen: 29.03.2029 (Innenausbau + Technik gem. Generalablaufplan_V5) Unter Berücksichtigung des Starttermins ist ein Montageterminplan vorzulegen und ggf. an Vorgaben des Architekten (4Bund) anzupassen. Die jeweils für die Einbringung und Montage benötigten Zeiten sind pro Gerät zu hinterlegen.

description: Hankinnan kohteena on Adoben käyttöoikeuksien jakelu- ja hallintapalvelu solmittavan hankintasopimuksen mukaisesti. Jakelu- ja hallintapalvelussa Toimittaja tarjoaa Adoben ohjelmistotuotteiden jakelukanavat ja sopimuksen mukaiset muut palvelut Tilaajalle perustuen Tilaajan ja tämän Asiakkaiden käyttämiin osto-ohjelmiin. Käytössä ovat hallinnon- ja sivistyspuolen VIP Marketplace- osto-ohjelmat (GOV ja EDU). Tilaajalla on oikeus valita ja vaihtaa osto-ohjelmaa sopimuskaudella, mikäli se nähdään tarpeelliseksi. Toimittaja sitoutuu jälleenmyymään käyttöoikeuksia Tilaajan valitsemilla osto-ohjelmilla, joista voidaan sopia sopimuksen voimassaoloaikana siten, että osto-ohjelma alkaa ennen sopimuksen päättymistä. Toimittajalta vaaditaan vähintään Gold Certified Reseller -status sekä oikeus jälleenmyydä tuotteita GOV- ja EDU -asiakasryhmille. Tilaajalla on tällä hetkellä käytössä Adoben VIP Marketplace -osto-ohjelmaan kuuluvia ohjelmistolisenssejä, joten erikoisosaaminen VIP Marketplace osto-ohjelmasta on myös hankinnan kohteeseen liittyvä perusvaatimus. Käyttöoikeuksien vuosipäivä on hallintopuolen osalta 17.3.2027 ja EDU-puolen osalta 7.6.2027. Tarjouskilpailun perusteella valitaan yksi (1) sopimuskumppani, jonka kanssa sopimus solmitaan. Kiinteä sopimuskausi on voimassa kolme (3) vuotta, minkä jälkeen sopimus voi jatkua toistaiseksi voimassaolevana sovituin irtisanomisehdoin.

title: MECHANICAL PREVENTATIVE MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT
description: NOTICE OF INTENT � SOLE-SOURCE ACQUISITION Notice No.: 75N98027Q00104 The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD), intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to Chesapeake System for mechanical preventive maintenance agreement. Description of the Requirement This preventative maintenance agreement is needed for the siemens software and remote monitoring system in the Centralized and Decentralized Aquatics Facilities. This preventative maintenance service includes emergency remote alarm monitoring which allows the Siemens 24/7 Service Center access to the emergency alarms that are associated with the aquatic system during the hours where husbandry staff is not on campus so the aquatic staff can be notified of any harmful or threatening situations that could compromise the health of the aquatic research animals. Without this service, the staff would have no means of knowing if any system was malfunctioning or any water quality parameter was cut of range during the hours that staff are not on campus. Siemens is the manufacturer and sole service provider for the NICHD Siemens Aquatic APOGEE InfeCenter system utilized in the facility. The Government intends to solicit from a single source pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The Siemens Industry APOGEE system is a proprietary software program designed to monitor and maintain critical environmental parameters associated with the NICHD aquatic research facilities. Siemens Industry is the sole manufacturer and service provider for this system, including all associated switches, relays, panels, hardware, and software. These components are owned, maintained, and serviced exclusively by Siemens due to the system�s unique proprietary communication protocols, which are not compatible with other systems or service providers. This preventative maintenance service also includes emergency remote alarm monitoring through Siemens� 24/7 Service Center, allowing aquatic staff to be notified of any system malfunctions or water quality parameters that fall outside acceptable ranges during hours when husbandry staff are not on campus. Without this service, there would be no reliable means of identifying or responding to potentially harmful conditions that could compromise the health and well-being of the aquatic research animals. Replacing the existing system or procuring services from another manufacturer would require significant changes to the facility�s existing infrastructure and monitoring equipment, void applicable Siemens warranties, and create substantial operational and financial burdens. Failure to maintain this service could result in the inability to properly operate the existing aquatic monitoring program, significant loss of research animals, and the potential loss of valuable research. Siemens Industry is the sole manufacturer and servicer for the Siemens APOGEE software. The switches, relays, and panels for the monitoring system on each facility�s system are also owned and maintained by Siemens. Response Information This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required preventive maintenance and remedial repair services for the specified instrument and meet all applicable technical and operational requirements. The Government will review timely submissions to determine whether another responsible source is capable of satisfying the requirement and whether a competitive acquisition is appropriate. The Government anticipates making an award after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source can satisfy the requirement. Capability statements must be submitted electronically to verne.griffin@nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on December 3, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98027Q00104 in the subject line of the submission.

Additional work includes construction of an access road, retaining wall, railing, and road gate; tieback design and tieback fabrication/installation for the retaining wall; and site restoration in accordance with the plans and specifications. Associated work includes concrete removal, excavation, dewatering, clearing and grubbing, and other incidental work necessary to provide a complete and usable project.The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. This acquisition will be competed as a 100% Small Business Set-Aside. The magnitude of construction is estimated to be between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000.Please be advised that this requirement is subject to change and may be revised or canceled at any time prior to award.

title: Germany – Architectural and related services – Generalsanierung mit Erweiterung Inklusionskindergarten in Lappersdorf. Architektenleistungen der Objektplanung Gebäude und Innenräume, Leistungsphasen 5 bis 8, gem. HOAI Teil 3 Abschnitt 1.
description: Der Markt Lappersdorf plant, den vorhandenen Inklusionskindergarten KGL mit 4 Kindergartengruppen zu sanieren und auf 7 Gruppen zu erweitern. Die Programmfläche beträgt insgesamt ca. 1600 qm. Der bestehende eingeschossige Kindergarten aus dem Baujahr 1970 an der Pielmühler Strasse wurde bereits mehrfach umgebaut und im Jahr 1990 erweitert. Der verputzte Mauerwerksbau hat Satteldächer mit unterschiedlichen Deckungen aus Zinkblech, Ziegel sowie teilweise mit einer PV-Anlage. Der Zustand des Kindergartens entspricht funktional nicht mehr dem Stand der Technik und muss saniert werden. Das Gebäude ist insbesondere energetisch und in Bezug auf Brandschutz sowie die Barrierefreiheit veraltet und muss entsprechend ertüchtigt werden. Für die geplante Generalsanierung und Erweiterung wurden die Leistungsphasen 1 - 3 bereits erbracht. Die Baugenehmigung ist beantragt. Das vorliegende VgV-Vergabeverfahren ist Grundlage für die Vergabe der Architektenleistungen der Ausführungsplanung, Vorbereitung und Mitwirkung bei der Vergabe und Objektüberwachung, also der Leistunsphasen 5 bis 8 gem. HOAI. Da eine Bewerbung des vorbefassten Büros nicht ausgeschlossen werden kann, werden zum Ausgleich des Informationsvorsprungs diverse Informationsunterlagen zur Verfügung gestellt, u.a. Planungsgrundlagen, Entwurfsplanung und Kosten. Für die Entwurfsplanung liegt das Nutzungsrecht am Urheberrecht beim Markt Lappersdorf. Die bestehenden 4 Kindergartengruppen sind während der Bauzeit ausgelagert und werden provisorisch in Containern auf dem naheliegenden Rathausparkplatz untergebracht. Die Auslagerung ist nicht Gegenstand des Auftrags. Die Außenanlagen des bestehenden Kindergartens werden während der Bauphase weiter als Freianlagen zum Spielen genutzt. Gegenstand des Auftrags sind die Architektenleistungen der Objektplanung Gebäude und Innenräume gem. HOAI Teil 3 Abschnitt 1, Leistungsphasen 5 bis 8. Der Auftraggeber rechnet für die Kostengruppen 300 und 400 mit Kosten von ca. 6,2 Mio. Euro einschl. Mehrwertsteuer und ordnet die Maßnahme der Honorarzone III zu. Eine Vergabe der Leistungen in Stufen wird vorbehalten. Aus der stufenweisen Beauftragung können keine zusätzlichen Honoraransprüche geltend gemacht werden. Die Planungen sind unmittelbar nach Auftragsvergabe zu beginnen. Voraussichtlich werden folgende Förderprogramme in Anspruch genommen: FAG-Förderung und KfW-Förderung. Betreiber des Kindergartens ist die Katholische Jugendfürsorge der Diözese Regensburg e.V.

title: CAWT PEACEPLUS EASY Project: Early Intervention Support for Children, Young People and Families presenting with Neurodevelopmental Needs (SHSCT Area)
description: This is a project supported by PEACEPLUS, a programme managed by the Special EU Programmes Body (SEUPB). The CAWT PEACEPLUS Early Intervention Support Youth Hubs (EASY) project aims to establish new cross border early intervention support services for families with children and young people presenting with traits consistent with a neurodevelopmental type need or who have been recently diagnosed with a neurodevelopmental condition. By providing help based on presenting need/symptoms, the project aims to improve outcomes for children, young people and their families by helping families' access appropriate support, based on needs at the right time and in the right place. title: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for Commercial Items Agile Professional Services (APS) Department of the Army
description: *** 11/23/2026: AMENDMENT 08 ISSUED - SEE SUMMARY OF AMENDMENT AT BOTTOM OF POSTING*** ***SUMMARY ONLY - SEE ATTACHED COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION DOCUMENT FOR FULL DETAIL*** APS _ Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Brief: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for Commercial Items Agile Professional Services ("APS�) Department of the Army Project Name: Agile Professional Services ("APS") Solicitation Number: W900KK-26-R-A023 NAICS Code: 541990 (All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services) Set-Aside: Total Small Business Set-Aside Contract Type: Labor Hours/T&M 1. General Information This combined synopsis/solicitation is issued by Army Contracting Command - APG - Orlando Division to procure Agile Professional Services ("APS"). The acquisition is structured to support critical technical and professional operations under a flexible framework, to be proposed and developed by the successful offeror. Key acquisition parameters include: � Set-Aside Status: 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. � Small Business Size Standard: $19.5M, or as defined by SBA regulations. � Primary NAICS Classification: 541990 � All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services. � Contract Vehicle Type: Labor Hours/T&M 2. Solicitation Details This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. This combined synopsis/solicitation is prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular FAC 2025-06, effective August 27, 2025.and DFARS Publication Notice (DPN) July 2, 2026. As described in the attached FAR 52.212-2, The Army will adopt aspects of FAR Part 15 evaluation procedures. Considering the novel, and commercial, nature of these services this is deemed necessary to balance fairness, transparency, and competition with the interests of expediency and flexibility 3. Description of Requirement CPE ST3 has a need for Agile Professional Services (APS) support services to provide the organization with the ability to augment its Military and Government Civilian workforce in order to execute its mission. The services will be limited to providing professional support services, under a Performance Based Services model, to CPE ST3 and CPE ST3 customers for limited requirements which are related to CPE ST3�s mission. Since its inception, CPE ST3 has relied on contractor support to conduct its mission in all phases of life cycle management due to insufficient personnel within the organization to successfully perform the required services. This model of a Government footprint with a scalable contractor workforce has enabled CPE ST3 to be very flexible and agile in its mission to support the changing needs of the Army. The services to be performed will include related activities in support of all aspects of providing responsive integrated and interoperable infrastructure for simulation, training, testing, and threat solutions. APS support services are required for effective, efficient, and responsive full lifecycle management of efforts to include, but not limited to: vision statements and doctrine, development of architectures, program support (e.g., acquisition and budget planning, business and financial programming and execution, modeling, simulation, simulator, training device, and instrumentation development, documentation, fielding and execution, system analysis and integration, integrated logistics support, strategic planning, contingency and mission support, security cooperation/international relations, program oversight, independent verification validation and test evaluation, prototype development, sustainment and operations, and analysis of emerging technologies support), and subject matter experts on military tactics, techniques, and procedures. Potential areas of growth are envisioned but not limited to be in the areas of Cyber and Information Warfare, Robotics, Unmanned Vehicles, Home Station Training, Multi-Sensory Simulation, Artificial Intelligence, Hypersonics, Directed Energy, Electronic Warfare, Autonomous Systems, Multi-Domain Integration, Target and Threat Systems, Environment Modeling, Human Performance Training, Security Cooperation, Nuclear Engineering, and Medical Training. The critical performance requirement is the successful development and transition of CPE ST3 from a traditional, staffing-based support model to a task-based, outcome-driven Agile delivery framework that is to be developed by the Performer. Success will be measured by the contractor's ability to develop and iterate, through performance under the resultant contract, a framework that both provides the following, and is able to be replicated across future requirements. 4. Period of Performance / Performance Locations: Total Performance Period shall not exceed 66-months: Base Period � (15-Mar-27 to 14-Sep-27) Agile Development and Transition In Option Period 1 � (15-Sep-27 to 14-Sep-28) � Enterprise Performance Option Period 2 � (15-Sep-28 to 14-Sep-29) � Enterprise Performance Option Period 3 � (15-Sep-29 to 14-Sep-30) � Enterprise Performance Option Period 4 � (15-Sep-30 to 14-Sep-31) � Enterprise Performance Option Period 5 � (15-Sep-31 to 14-Mar-32) � Enterprise Performance and Transition Out Option Period 6 � (15-Mar-32 to 14-Sep-32) � Option to Extend the Term of Service under FAR 52.217-8 * Work will be performed at Government facilities, Contractor facilities, and Remote locations. Primary Government sites include Orlando, FL, and Redstone Arsenal, AL (including 24/7 operations). Additional Government sites include: Fort Campbell, KY; Fort Hood, TX; Fort Drum, NY; Fort Irwin, CA; Fort Polk, LA; Fort Rucker, AL; Fort Bragg, NC; Hohenfels, Germany; and Camp Humphreys, South Korea. 5. Applicable FAR Provisions/Provisions: See Attachment 7. The provisions and clauses apply to this acquisition and are incorporated by reference or full text as applicable. The full text of the FAR and DFARS clauses may be accessed electronically at https://www.acquisition.gov/. 6. Proposal Submission Instructions Phase II responses to this solicitation are due by 3 December 2026 / 10:00am (Eastern). Submission due dates for all subsequent Phases will be issued via Advisory Notifications / Invitations. a. Electronic Submission Requirement All proposals must be submitted electronically via the Department of Defense Secure Access File Exchange (DoD SAFE) application at https://safe.apps.mil . Hardcopy submissions or proposals sent directly via standard email will not be accepted. b. DoD SAFE Link Upon issuance of Phase II Notification / Invitation, the Government will be issuing each respective Offeror (2) DoD SAFE links. Links will be sent to the POC identified in the Phase I Cover Letter: DoD SAFE Link #1 - Pick Up - JIRA Data: Each Offeror will receive an email from DoD SAFE with a link in which to download all the JIRA Data and Instructions. DoD SAFE Link #2 - Drop Off - Phase II Proposal Submittal: Each Offeror will receive a secondary email from DoD SAFE with a link to upload all their respective documents for Phase II, including the final PowerPoint Presentation and their attendee list for Oral Presentations. Link Validity: Once the Government issues the pick-up and drop-off, each Offeror will receive automated emails from DoD SAFE containing the unique links and instructions. These links are valid for exactly 14 days from the date of receipt. WARNING: The Government will not be held responsible for late proposals resulting from an offeror's failure to submit a drop-off by the established deadline. c. Submission Protocol Upon receipt of the automated DoD SAFE email link: Click the link inside the automated email to access the secure upload portal. Upload all required solicitation attachments, ensuring they are named clearly.

description: This is a Sources Sought Notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of qualified sources and whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. Womack Army Medical Center (WAMC) located on Fort Bragg, NC has a requirement for custom-fabricated dental laboratory materials, surgical guides, prosthetic appliances, and incidental non-personal technical support services (Hands-Off-Patient Chairside Prosthetic Conversion and Digital Dental Planning) needed for Dental and Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (OMFS) Procedures, to include any potential prosthetic connection components manufactured and/or distributed by the Contractor. description: The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity-Healthcare Contracting-Division San Antonio (DHACA-HCD-SA) is issuing this Sources Sought Notice on behalf of Brooke Army Medical Center (BAMC) to conduct market research for interested vendors to provide non-personal Laundry Services for consolidated bulk and piece laundry services. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT � This is a Sources Sought Notice and is issued solely for information and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ) or a promise to issue an RFQ in the future. Solicitations are not available at this time and requests for a solicitation will not receive a response. Not responding to this Sources Sought Notice does not preclude participation in any future Request for Quote (RFQ), should one be issued. It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this requirement. The Government will utilize responses to this notice in formulating its acquisition strategy. If the Government does not receive sufficient information in response to this notice to verify the potential for competition exists, it is possible that a sole-source contract, supported by a Justification and Approval document, will be issued to support the Government's requirement. DHACA-HCD-SA is seeking eligible businesses capable of providing non-personal services to provide Consolidated Bulk and Piece Laundry Services in support of BAMC. Address the following questions with your submission: Company name, Unique Entity ID, CAGE code, and point of contact information (including phone number and email address), and socio-economic category(ies) as related to 812320 Drycleaning and Laundry Services (except Coin-Operated). Capability Statement (limited to ten pages), describing how your company meets the below objectives additional proof (such as product literature and locations where the system is currently installed) where appropriate: We would also appreciate your company�s feedback on the requirements outlined in the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS), including any impediments to your firm proposing or any concerns you have regarding the ability to provide a fair and reasonable price Question to address: Do you have the capability to perform linen pickup and drop-off twice per week? Once per week? If not, what is the maximum frequency you can support? What is the distance from your facility to BAMC? If your company is not within the BAMC/San Antonio area, would you consider a subcontracting arrangement with a local drycleaning/laundry firm? How would you secure the subcontract relationship prior to proposing? Is the distance to the facility for pickup and delivery prohibitive of your company proposing on this requirement at a fair and reasonable price? If so, are there any changes that the government should consider to increase your ability to provide a proposal and maintain a reasonable price? Would allowing a combination of linen rental to supplement the laundering requirement potentially make this requirement more or less attractive to your company? Please explain why. If a linen rental program was offered, would a reduced pickup/drop-off frequency (e.g., once every two weeks) be more feasible? Please provide the duration and ROM for rental that you expect would be required, (e.g., linens sufficient for one week beyond what MTF already owns at a cost of $XXXX per week) What other factors, if any, would prevent your company from submitting a proposal for this requirement? (Examples: inability to meet security requirements, facility limitations, etc.) Beyond those outlined above, are there any specific challenges or concerns you foresee in fulfilling this requirement, given the scope of work and delivery schedule? title: Water Treatment Chemicals, Testing, Monitoring, and Reporting- Sources Sought Notice / Request for Information
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Water Treatment Chemicals, Testing, Monitoring, and Reporting BPA Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) Notice Type Sources Sought / Request for Information / Market Research Agency Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) Contracting Office Federal Bureau of Prisons, Facilities Management Branch 320 First Street NW Washington, DC 20534 Purpose This is a Sources Sought Notice issued solely for market research purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) is seeking qualified contractors capable of providing water treatment chemicals, water testing, treatment recommendations, reporting, and related support services for federal correctional institutions nationwide, under a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA). This notice is not a solicitation and does not constitute a commitment by the Government to award a contract or BPA. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with responding to this notice. The contractor shall furnish all personnel, chemicals, testing equipment, laboratory services, transportation, reporting systems, technical support, and related resources necessary to support boiler water systems, chiller water loops, cooling towers, and domestic water systems at participating BOP facilities. Services include water sampling and analysis, chemical treatment programs, Legionella testing, domestic water testing, water quality reporting, corrective action recommendations, trend analysis, regulatory compliance support, and maintenance of a secure online reporting portal. Contractors shall provide monthly and quarterly reports and maintain water quality treatment programs designed to reduce corrosion, scaling, biological growth, and other operational risks associated with institutional water systems. The requirement includes support for multiple BOP institutions located throughout the United States. Contractors should carefully consider the geographic distribution of performance locations and demonstrate their ability to provide timely service, technical support, testing, and delivery of treatment chemicals to institutions nationwide. Respondents shall identify any planned subcontracting arrangements and provide examples of water treatment, water testing, boiler treatment, cooling tower treatment, Legionella monitoring, or similar services performed directly by their organization as the prime contractor. Experience performed solely by subcontractors or teaming partners should be separately identified. Any future small business set-aside acquisition resulting from this requirement will be subject to the applicable limitations on subcontracting requirements contained in FAR 52.219-14 and 13 CFR �125.6. Respondents should describe how they would comply with these requirements if awarded a contract. Vendors should carefully review the draft requirements before submitting a response. The Government is seeking capability information from firms that can directly perform and support the full scope of services, including water testing, chemical treatment, reporting, and compliance support across multiple correctional institutions. Responses that do not address the firm's ability to meet the requirements outlined herein may be considered less useful for market research purposes. Background The Federal Bureau of Prisons seeks a contractor capable of providing comprehensive water treatment services and chemical products for institutions operating: Steam boiler systems Hot water boiler systems Chilled water systems Cooling towers Domestic water systems The contractor would be responsible for supporting institutions nationwide through testing, treatment recommendations, chemical supply, reporting, and compliance monitoring. Information contained within the draft Statement of Work serves as the basis for this market research effort. Scope of Requirements The Government is interested in determining industry capability to provide the following services: 1. Water Treatment Chemicals Provide water treatment chemicals and related application support for: Boiler systems Chiller water loops Cooling towers Domestic water systems The contractor must be capable of supporting multiple geographically dispersed correctional institutions. 2. Boiler Water Testing and Treatment Provide: Monthly testing of boiler water systems Written treatment reports Corrective recommendations Chemical treatment programs Corrosion prevention measures Contractors must be capable of implementing treatment recommendations and supplying required chemicals within fifteen (15) calendar days of test results. 3. Chiller Loop and Cooling Tower Testing Provide: Monthly seasonal testing Water quality analysis Treatment recommendations Corrosion prevention services Cooling tower chemical treatment Contractors must provide solutions to maintain water quality and system efficiency. 4. Domestic Water and Legionella Testing Provide quarterly testing at active inmate housing institutions, including: Legionella E. coli Lead Arsenic Nitrates PFAS pH Mineral content Contractors shall identify deficiencies and provide corrective recommendations. 5. Online Reporting Platform Provide and maintain a secure web-based platform capable of: Institution-level user access Regional and Central Office oversight access Monthly and quarterly report storage Historical trending analysis Water quality dashboards Chemical usage tracking Compliance reporting Corrective action tracking The platform should support enterprise-wide visibility across all participating institutions. Anticipated NAICS Code The Government is considering the following NAICS codes and seeks industry feedback regarding the most appropriate code: NAICS Description 325998 All Other Miscellaneous Chemical Product and Preparation Manufacturing 541380 Testing Laboratories and Services 561210 Facilities Support Services 221310 Water Supply and Irrigation Systems Respondents are encouraged to recommend alternative NAICS codes if more appropriate.
